clue.text: Desires bringing problems for 'Arry

indicators.note: 'Arry is a Cockney Harry, who drops his aitches, so the word is said without its opening H

parts.note: hitches are snags or problems

explanation.surface: Someone's cravings are landing a Cockney chap called Harry in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words; 'Arry is how a Londoner says Harry, so HITCHES loses its H. Cockney is the working-class dialect of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Itches are strong urges or cravings, a synonym for desires.

clue.text: Artist coming to church in attempt to establish window pattern?

indicators.note: in places the artist and church inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A painter joins a church's effort to design a stained-glass window.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the ornamental stonework pattern in the upper part of a Gothic window.

clue.text: Port's making frameworks for vessels

definitions.meaning: Hull is an English port city on the Humber
the main bodies of ships, their outer shells

explanation.surface: A harbour town makes the shells of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 's as 'is', so 'Port's making' becomes 'Hull's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hulls are the structural bodies of ships, and Hull is a Yorkshire port, both senses fitting.

clue.text: Street work — look at something taking time

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to watch is to look at

explanation.surface: Roadworks are being observed by someone who is timing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch times events, taking time in the sense of measuring it.

clue.text: Something in a music bar here again — attend!

parts.note: back means returned, here again
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: Someone back in a music bar is urged to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbeat is the accent on the second and fourth beats within a bar of music.

clue.text: Their skins pose risks? Crazy!

definitions.meaning: a fruit whose discarded peel is the classic thing to slip on
mad, nuts, as an informal adjective

explanation.surface: A warning that some peel is dangerous, and an exclamation at the madness of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit's skins are the comic slipping hazard, and the plural slang 'gone bananas' means crazy.

clue.text: Attractive person quietly leaving knockout match

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for quietly goes out of the match

parts.note: a cup tie is a match in a knockout football competition
P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: A good-looking spectator slips out of a cup game early.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a match in a knockout football competition such as the FA Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is informal for a charming, good-looking person.

clue.text: Second set correct? Wrong set for most intelligent

parts.note: B is the second grade or set, as in a B team
right means correct

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the second set are put out of order

explanation.surface: A tennis player queries whether the second set was right, and is told the wrong set was given for the cleverest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightest is the superlative of bright, clever, so it means most intelligent.

clue.text: Member of tribe has point of view not English — Scotsman?

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for English is left out of the point of view

parts.note: an angle is a point of view
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A tribesman with an opinion that isn't English might be Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic tribe; an Anglian is one of them.

clue.text: Futile message offering to give everything away?

definitions.text: message offering to give everything away?
definitions.meaning: read literally, an offer of the whole lot at no price

explanation.surface: A pointless notice offering to hand over all one's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes effort wasted in vain; literally it would offer the lot free of charge.

clue.text: One of two American brothers, awful whingers

indicators.note: awful hints the whingers are badly treated, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a pair of American siblings who complain terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: George and Ira Gershwin were the American brothers who wrote songs and musicals together.

clue.text: Foul kitchen — cook finally dismissed from particular community

indicators.note: foul suggests the remaining letters are fouled up and rearranged
dismissed means that letter is sent out of the word kitchen
finally picks the closing letter of cook

explanation.surface: A dirty kitchen gets its chef sacked by a local group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes K from cook; 'dismissed' removes it from KITCHEN to leave ITCHEN, which 'Foul' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic describes a group sharing culture or descent, so it labels a particular community.

clue.text: Some 'daddy', nasty sort of ruler

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sneering description of a cruel father figure as a nasty kind of boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynast is a ruler from a hereditary line, a member of a dynasty.

clue.text: Navigator in car leading smug group

indicators.note: leading puts the car word in front of the rest

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
pi is informal for sanctimonious or smug, short for pious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A sat-nav sits in a car heading a self-satisfied crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is British slang for self-righteous or smug.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot steers a craft automatically, so it acts as a navigator.

clue.text: Officer in twilled fabric meeting social worker

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A uniformed officer dressed in serge meets a welfare employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a rank of non-commissioned officer in the army or police.

clue.text: Nicer pet I trained to be award-winner?

indicators.note: trained hints the words are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog owner hopes training will make the pet a prize-winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient receives something, so the winner of an award is an example.

clue.text: Revolutionary embraced by fools and jerks

indicators.note: embraced by puts the revolutionary inside the word for fools

parts.note: twits are fools
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel is hugged by idiots and idiots alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitches are small sudden movements, jerks used as a plural noun or verb.

clue.text: Punishment? Explain the thing that caused it

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is to scold or punish them

definitions.text: Explain the thing that caused it
definitions.meaning: a request for the reason or purpose behind something

explanation.surface: Someone being punished asks why.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'give someone what for' means a scolding, and the phrase also literally asks for a reason.

clue.text: Employment in wicked activities? Such may give one a headache

definitions.text: Such may give one a headache

indicators.note: in puts the employment word inside the wicked activities

parts.note: sins are wicked acts
use is employment

explanation.surface: Using wicked pastimes may leave you with a sore head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are the air cavities in the skull whose congestion causes headaches.

clue.text: Hazel has this funny act in front of relations

indicators.note: in front of puts the reworked act before the relations
funny suggests the act is played oddly, its letters rearranged

parts.note: kin are relations

explanation.surface: A woman called Hazel performs a comic routine for her family.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel tree bears catkins, the dangling flower spikes, so this is something it has.

clue.text: Sixth sense within one of the other five?

parts.note: in means within
sight is one of the five ordinary senses

explanation.surface: A sixth sense wonders if it lives inside one of the regular five.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is intuitive understanding, which a sixth sense provides.

clue.text: One in tent wants hot, not cold, food box

indicators.note: hot, not cold means the cold letter is swapped for the hot one

parts.note: a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: A camper wants a warm meal rather than a cold one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker basket for carrying food, as on a picnic.

clue.text: Nonconformist and bishop in dance

indicators.note: in places the bishop inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman who dissents joins a dance with a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel defies convention, a synonym for a nonconformist.

clue.text: Restrictive practice in business? I stop men working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A union boss halting the workforce is accused of a restrictive practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouring relatives in jobs, which restricts who a business hires.

clue.text: Fabric, not quite enough for small room

indicators.note: not quite enough for means the word falls one letter short at its end

parts.note: the toilet is often called the smallest room

explanation.surface: There isn't quite enough cloth to cover a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a light cotton or linen cloth, often printed with scenes.

clue.text: Awkward brute is interrupting office task, a delaying tactic

indicators.note: interrupting puts the rearranged letters inside the office task

parts.note: filing is a routine office job

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters of brute is are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy thug gets in the way of the paperwork, holding everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' looks like a description of the brute, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Filibustering is prolonged speechmaking to stall a vote in a legislature.

clue.text: Troubles after President initially talks foolishly

indicators.note: after puts the troubles word behind that letter
initially picks the first letter of President

parts.note: to rattle someone is to trouble or unsettle them

explanation.surface: Political troubles follow once the President starts talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter idly or foolishly.

clue.text: Handle last bit of wordy agreement

parts.note: to treat something is to handle or deal with it

indicators.note: last bit of takes the closing letter of wordy

explanation.surface: An instruction to deal with the final part of a verbose contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.
